That sweep keeps only rows whose current action and target both lie inside top-CC, so the scored subset itself shrinks with CC—by up to 65.5% of rows at the narrow budgets. Re-running it on a fixed row set (out-of-catalog goals masked to an always-offered unknown class) leaves the shape intact and the gap smaller: net +0.5 points at C=154C{=}154 to +1.2 at C=6,750C{=}6{,}750 (a dip to +0.3 at C=512C{=}512) over strictly paired candidate lists—identical options for both arms on rows whose target lies on that list; charging each arm for the options it cannot name instead flips the sign at the two narrow budgets (−1.8-1.8, −1.2-1.2). The class-space advantage therefore ends wider across the sweep (non-monotonically) and, in the row-filtered and paired means, never crosses over on the measured axis (top-CC up to 6,750; outside the noise-level ties, the charging-convention flips above and the contrary small-catalog slices—the evaluation subset at its 275-name training catalog and API-Bank—are the exceptions disclosed in Figure 10): even at the widest tested budget (C=6,750C{=}6{,}750, 43.8×43.8\times the SOC’s 154 option names), a shared class vocabulary is the better parameterization of the next-hop choice. The edge-ID variant may still pay where option names carry no meaning (Sun et al., 2026b)—that regime remains open. Scope. The readout has no mechanism for multi-step internal search (the single-pass design of Cheng et al. (2026) likewise cannot carry intermediate results through); long detours are delegated to the graph and to LLM escalation at genuine unknowns. All typed-model timing is batch-1 GPU wall clock (NVIDIA H20, App. B) except the in-vivo zero-shot pipeline, measured on CPU; service and judge latencies are measured in vivo under production load and vary with it.

Data availability and governance. The logs behind §6 are production security-operations records of a deployment that is not ours to release, and no human-subjects data were collected for this study. The derived, non-identifying artifacts that back every reported number—frozen per-decision predictions, the aggregation and audit scripts, and the per-experiment receipts—can be made available on request. The public bundle is sufficient to re-derive every corpus-level aggregate reported here—episode, session, split and per-slice counts, the held-out option-space mean and its 3,5683{,}568-of-3,8753{,}875 coverage, the catalog size and the fold-event totals—while the pre-fold trace count, the semantic families and the model-level results require the internal export. Authorization, retention and re-identification boundaries, the human review roles around the sessions, and catalog change management remain properties of the deployment that produced the logs: what this paper states about them is limited to what the stripped export can show, and nothing here should be read as a governance assessment of that deployment.

10 Conclusion

Logs already contain an organization’s workflow knowledge; NIOCIS turns them into a graph whose transition set runs a long tail and whose node vocabulary converges at rates a zero-parameter occupancy null already predicts (E1), and pairs it with a typed router that reads next-hop decisions off that graph in one forward pass, escalating only its own uncertainty to the slow, expensive path. The loop closes: every executed walk becomes gated training signal. On 1,615 production episodes the pieces separately hold—quantified node-vocabulary convergence of the induced action graph (E1); feature-MLP readouts reaching 32.8% agreement with the deployed fleet (35.6% within the declared space), with the hidden-state probe variant holding 30.7% at a 10 ms per-state encoder pass plus a linear head against 2.2 s LLM hops, and out-agreeing the re-prompted MIMO Pro V2.6 stand-in (tool-result-stripped, zero-shot) on the same states (E2–E3)—a transfer-floor comparison, not a capability ceiling: the stand-in is never fine-tuned. Route-level replay keeps the typed layer in the agreement/cost corner while exposing the accept/escalate hybrid’s calibration failure as a negative result (E3). A self-evolution loop’s rollback gate scores every candidate while the loop absorbs the flipped labels of one update batch (12% of that batch’s labels corrupted—about 0.3% of the 12,613-decision base) without firing rollback on the plotted seed-0 chain (E4). Across ten seeded chains the gate refuses 13 of the 40 candidate updates, in 6 of the 10 chains. An external replication runs the same fold over 60,613 public cases, where loop mass reaches 99.4% on an instrumented software session and 1.4% on traffic fines; node discovery flattens wherever catalogs are small (E5); NIOCIS’s decision construction carries over to a 7,318-name tool catalog, where a transition table isolates what the feature MLP contributes beyond order-≤\leq3 memorized transitions; on the case streams an occupancy null shows node saturation is combinatorics, conditional on the observed label supports. The invitation is concrete: drop your logs into the fold pipeline and measure your own saturation curve.

Reproducibility statement

All model experiments run on the released pipeline in experiments/ inside an nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.03-py3 container on a remote host with 2×2\times NVIDIA H20 (GPUs 0/1) against frozen artifacts in experiments/real/ (episodes.jsonl, e2_*.jsonl, e1_saturation.json, e2_results.json, e2_layaprobe_results.json, e2_laya_results.json, gpu_latency.json, e3_replay.json, e4_rsi.json, e8_slices.json, outcome_labels_v2.jsonl, outcome_labels.jsonl, corpus_census.json, e2_laya_raw.json, pub_e1_results.json, pub_sweep_results.json, pub_coupon.json, pub_markov_results.json, e2_meta.json, e2_results_cpu_local.json, forensics_stats.json, gold_30.json, audit_sample.json, outcome_label_summary.json, outcome_label_v2_summary.json, tool_parse_report.json, tool_manifest.json, pub_fetch_manifest.json, e3_mimo_stream.json and every public stream’s *_e2_results.json/*_e2_meta.json pair; the typed-choice feature tensor feats_laya_cls.npz, assembled from the sharded extraction passes by assemble_feats.py, is a further frozen input). The eight stream names are apibank, bpi12, bpi17, helpdesk, receipt, roadtraffic, toolbench_train and toolbench_eval. The experiments/addendum/ artifacts (feat_lat_results.json, e4_rsi_multi.json, pub_sweep_fixed_results.json, e3_replay_multi.json, e9_graph_necessity.json, e9b_node_prior_curkey.json, e9b_node_prior_nodekey.json) are likewise frozen inputs (the E9/E9b option-space arms are produced by e9_graph_necessity.py and e9b_node_prior.py, which read only the frozen feature tensor, the derived decision streams and the frozen probe reference, and which reconcile to e2_layaprobe_results.json as a parity check), and tables/*.tex and figure PDFs are regenerated from these artifacts by make_tab_corpus.py, render_figs_tabs_real.py and render_pub.py.

The raw corpus export is internal SOC telemetry and cannot be redistributed; the derived corpus joins the code release in pseudonymized form (release/)—the 154 action labels map to stable opaque codes, identifiers are hashed under a private salt, and tool-argument payloads and free-text rationales are stripped, with independent leak gates keeping the result clean (verify_release.py); the label mapping and the salt are withheld together with the raw export. Two public-data chains extend the pipeline beyond the SOC corpus and re-run from a clean host with one command each: chain_pub.sh (fetch →\to XES parse →\to fold statistics →\to tables/figures) and the tool-trajectory chain (pub_tool_fetch.py →\to pub_tool_parse.py →\to pub_e2_build.py →\to pub_e2_train.py, with the two analysis add-ons pub_markov.py and pub_coupon.py writing pub_markov_results.json and pub_coupon.json); every downloaded artifact is pinned by sha256 in its fetch manifest (App. B), and both pipelines fold through the identical rules (fold_rules.py, imported by parse_real_corpus.py, pub_e1.py and pub_e2_build.py; e2_build.py carries the same rules as its original fold_events), with a lineage self-test in pub_e2_build.py asserting its decision construction agrees with the fold kind-for-kind. The JSONL schema and fold tooling document the rest of what a replication needs: parse_real_corpus.py consumes any Langfuse-style observations export; the derived-outcome rule of §5 is a pure function of the parsed call structure (labels, arguments and ordering), reproduced by label_real_v2.py on the internal episodes.jsonl; the derived outcomes ship precomputed (outcome_labels_v2.jsonl) because the release strips the argument payloads the rule reads. Models: MIMO Pro V2.6 and DS V4.1 Flash are production services behind our gateway (§5); Laya 0.3.21 is public (pypi package laya, checkpoint convaiinnovations/laya via ModelScope), loaded from a local snapshot. Seeded fits fix random_state=0 and torch seeds 0–4; the hidden-state probe and the E4 refits train on the full 12,613-decision train split (plus, for the E4 refits, the batches accepted so far; an earlier 6,000-row subsample of the train split was retired before the reported runs; see the released e2_laya_probe.py) and all arms evaluate on the full test split (3,875 decisions). Timing is wall-clock batch-1 on GPU or in-vivo service latency and will vary by host and load. The one synthetic element (E4’s 12% corruption injection) is regenerated from its stated seed by the E4 script.

The code release and the pseudonymized derived corpus (release/) are available at https://github.com/geilihan/niocis, with a per-file MANIFEST.sha256; the derived corpus is released under CC BY 4.0.

Appendix A: fold statistics of the production corpus

The fold of §4 decomposes the 22,192 logged tool calls into 15,704 advance (forward) hops and 6,488 loop events (29.2% of steps). The 4,124 retry events arrive in 2,164 same-label repeat runs (a run of k≥2k\geq 2 consecutive identical labels contributes k−1k-1 retry events, so the length classes sum to 2,164 runs, contributing 4,124 retry events): 1,394 runs of length 2 (median length 2), a smooth decay (354 of length 3, 147 of length 4, 102 of length 5) and a thin tail of 167 runs of lengths 6 to 20 (20 consecutive same-label steps at the maximum). The 2,364 back events return to an earlier kept label at short-but-real distances (steps between the target’s previous occurrence and the return): 681 at ≤\leq1, 666 at 2–3, 553 at 4–8, 464 at 9+. Pair roles across the fold: 2,315 distinct pairs fire as first-visit forward transfers, 702 as returns (481 in both roles, 221 exclusively returns). Domain slices carry distinct closure behavior: detection closes 1,001/1,174 episodes (85%), response 62/245 (25%), recognition 7/54 (13%), protection 0/139—protection-stage sessions in this window hand off to sibling stages rather than declare completion (a real stage-behavior property of the deployment, not a labeling artifact; the derived labels and their validation are in §5). The one synthetic element is E4’s corruption model: round 3 flips 12% of update labels to a uniformly drawn non-target option—the draw is seeded by the script’s per-round RNG (RandomState(100+round), i.e. 103 for round 3)—a deliberate stand-in for upstream policy regressions. The multi-chain study quoted in the E4 figure caption runs ten refit chains: five coupled seed offsets (the torch init, the corruption draw and the validation-split permutation all shifted together) run as two 5-chain arms—one under the row-level stream split (seed offsets 0/1000/2000/3000/4000) and one under the whole-trace split (1000–5000; four of the five offsets shared). Each chain makes four candidate updates, so the study reports 13 refusals in 40 attempts over 6 of the 10 chains, with held-out accuracy averaging 30.3% →\to 31.0% (±0.5\pm 0.5 points) and an unpaired 0.02-point gap between the arms (0.09 points on the four shared offsets). Three of the ten chains dip below their previous committed score mid-study (two of those below their base fit) before recovering; every chain ends at or above its base fit. Results are in e4_rsi_multi.json (Reproducibility).

Appendix B: services and statistical details

The opponent (MIMO Pro V2.6) and the judge (DS V4.1 Flash) are served through our production gateway (vLLM backend; both are reasoning models that emit reasoning traces; decoding at temperature 0 with a 2,048-token completion budget). In-vivo call latencies appear in §6; smoke probes on tiny next-hop prompts run at p50 0.5 s (MIMO Pro V2.6) and 0.45 s (DS V4.1 Flash), growing with prompt and reasoning length (episode-level judge calls in §5 ran at p50 2.0 s, p90 5.6 s). The typed encoder’s backbone is Laya 0.3.21 with the convaiinnovations/laya checkpoint (ModernBERT-large encoder; marker-position decision head; an accept/escalate head with cost ratio escalate 0.5 versus wrong 3.0—matching the gap metric’s c3=3c_{3}{=}3 wrong-hop weight, which does not price escalations). Its shipped per-bucket decision temperatures include one out-of-range entry (choice:11+ =0.1=0.1, outside the library’s stated [0.5,5][0.5,5] range), so reported confidences use a scalar temperature refit by validation NLL for the zero-shot arm (all trained arms report raw masked-renorm confidence). That refit is unbounded: its optimum sits at whatever ceiling the grid imposes—T=3.0T{=}3.0 on the published eight-point grid and still T=1000T{=}1000 on a 60-point grid spanning 0.30.3–10001000—so the arm’s ECE-15 is grid-dependent (0.0310.031 against 0.0100.010) while its argmax and risk–coverage curve are unchanged. The hidden-state probe attaches a linear head to the encoder’s designated readout position—the pooled position the checkpoint’s own action head reads—and trains with CE versus CE-plus-Brier (Adam Kingma & Ba, 2015, 90-epoch fits for both objectives, batch 512—the released e2_laya_probe.py defaults) on the full 12,613-decision train split, with 5 seeds (0–4) for error bars (the feature-MLP readouts use 60-epoch fits over these seeds; the E4 and slice refits reuse the probe’s frozen encoder features with 60-epoch fits). Trained readout time budgets: feature arms fit in seconds on CPU; the probe’s one-time encoder extraction covers the full train/test splits (12,613 + 3,875 decisions) in 512-text chunks on GPU (throughput is host-specific). Model latency is wall-clock batch-1 on one NVIDIA H20 (in the nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.03-py3 container): typed-choice head predict 19.5 ms p50 (encoder included) over 17 declared options, the measured prompt’s count (50 warm trials; held-out states declare 40.2 options on average), bare encoder forward 10.0 ms p50 (the probe’s marginal per-state cost), and, in vivo and on CPU, 0.30 s p50 per state for the full Laya typed-choice pipeline (the zero-shot arm) (gpu_latency.json, e2_laya_results.json); service latencies vary under production load.

Public corpus provenance (E5).

Six event logs, fetched 2026-09-29 from their canonical hosts (some via pinned mirrors) and pinned by sha256 (pub_fetch_manifest.json): receipt, roadtraffic and helpdesk (pm4py-core test fixtures Berti et al., 2023 via the gh-proxy mirror), BPIC’12 (pm4py bpic2012.xes.gz), BPIC’17 and the Statechart Workbench software session (the 4TU file service; session log of Leemans (2018)). The tool-trajectory arm uses API-Bank (Li et al., 2023) (263 scenario files from AlibabaResearch/DAMO-ConvAI) and ToolBench (Qin et al., 2023) toolllama_G123_dfs chains (Adorg/ToolBench mirror on hf-mirror.com; 300 eval and 26,999 train trajectories), sha256-pinned in tool_manifest.json. Two candidate corpora were deliberately dropped rather than approximated—Zenodo discovery only surfaced a course homework scaffold for the Sepsis cases log of Mannhardt (2016) and a paper’s inputs.zip bundle for BPIC’11 (2011 BPI Challenge van Dongen, 2011)—and the xLAM 60k function-calling corpus (Liu et al., 2024) stays behind a HuggingFace LFS gate that denies anonymous fetches; no domestic mirror hosts that corpus. All three are simply absent: a missing row beats uncertain lineage. A builder-correction ledger accompanies the pipeline: URLs are verified against host APIs before hardcoding; extension-less 4TU links are typed by content magic; Content-Length and full gzip/zip integrity checks caught two silently truncated downloads (17.6 MB of 29.7 MB and 6.8 MB of 147 MB) before any number was computed from them; per-URL watchdogs guard against resolver hangs; and an XES trace-ID fallback covers software logs (which label traces concept:instance, not concept:name). Every reported number travels through verified, integrity-checked local copies.

Transition-table baseline.

Contexts over the traced node flow (orders 0–3) are counted on the training fold of each of the nine decision streams (SOC; API-Bank, BPIC’12, BPIC’17, helpdesk, receipt, roadtraffic and the two ToolBench streams); each order interpolates down to the training marginal with a cascading weight λ=wrem​nctx/(nctx+3)\lambda=w_{\mathrm{rem}}\,n_{\mathrm{ctx}}/(n_{\mathrm{ctx}}{+}3) (wremw_{\mathrm{rem}}: weight left unspent by higher orders, cascading 3→\to2→\to1, residue to the training marginal) and the argmax is restricted to the declared options (the deployed masked-renorm gate). Two scorings bracket each stream. The verbatim majority arm (raw per-node argmax)—scored raw and option-masked (a hit only when the argmax lands in the options)—recovers the §5 majority arm to the digit and matches every other stream’s identically-built look-up-table (LUT) arm exactly; the interpolated tables (an interpolated n-gram with backoff semantics—the backoff Markov) gate before scoring. For the majority arm, test accuracy equals its option-masked accuracy on all nine streams (pub_markov_results.json): option-gating never removes a correct majority prediction. The label catalog is treated as known (the class index covers every corpus label, held-out names included, so no action target is out of vocabulary). The public row encoding would bucket one at <stop>, and the edge-ID arms map training-fold-unseen edge targets to <unk_edge>; option sets and edge identifiers come from the training fold only.

Occupancy-null computation.

The dashed occupancy null of Figure 7a evaluates 𝔼⁡[D⁡(m)]\mathbb{E}[D(m)] at the same subsample sizes from per-label case supports alone—no fitted parameters (pub_coupon.json); its p50-versus-expectation comparison carries two residual components by design: the 20-draw median sampling noise of the panels and any mean-versus-median mismatch (𝔼⁡[D⁡(m)]\mathbb{E}[D(m)] need not equal the p50).

Catalog-size sweep (the edge-pays-at-scale hypothesis, §9).

pub_sweep.py holds the fold, features and training procedure fixed while shrinking the option vocabulary to the top-CC actions by train frequency, scoring only in-catalog decisions and rebuilding the option graph and edge vocabulary inside the catalog. Sweep budgets are bounded by each corpus’s training vocabulary: the five process logs contribute single points at their training vocabularies (11 to 27 names, |Δ|≤0.21|\Delta|\leq 0.21 points, noise-level ties) and ToolBench contributes the axis: the class-space readout beats the edge-ID readout at every budget (C=154C{=}154: 61.5% versus 60.6%; C=512C{=}512: 54.3 versus 53.7; C=2,048C{=}2{,}048: 47.6 versus 46.5; C=6,750C{=}6{,}750: 43.2 versus 41.9). Training floors: the 335-row API-Bank training fold and the 154-name slice of the evaluation subset fall below the sweep’s 500-train/50-test guard, so those rows are skipped.

The induced graph read as a discovered model.

For completeness we report the four standard discovery dimensions for the induced graph (§​2\lx@sectionsign\ref{sec:related}), with conventions stated because they are convention-dependent: fitness is the share of traces whose every consecutive kept pair is a model edge, with a token-replay flavour (1−unmatched pairs/pairs1-\text{unmatched pairs}/\text{pairs}); precision is the escaping-edge form (ETConformance style: 1−∑escaping/∑enabled1-\sum\text{escaping}/\sum\text{enabled} over trace prefixes, where escaping counts enabled outgoing edges not taken); generalization is the counting approximation (1−mean​ 1/visits1-\text{mean}\,1/\sqrt{\text{visits}} over model elements); simplicity is reported as counts (143 nodes with outgoing edges, 2,517 edges—1,944 forward, 573 recovery—mean out-degree 17.6). The graph is induced from the train fold, so in-sample readings are degenerate by construction (trace- and token-level fitness 1.0001.000); on held-out folds token-level fitness is 0.9020.902 (val) and 0.9130.913 (test, unmatched pairs 307/3,530307/3{,}530), trace-level fitness 0.6210.621 and 0.5910.591, escaping-edge precision 0.0220.022 and 0.0210.021, and generalization is 0.6250.625 at node level against 0.2670.267 at edge level. The permissive precision is structural: each state enables its entire declared option set (|A⁡(v)|¯=40.2\bar{|A(v)|}=40.2), so precision tracks 1/|A⁡(v)|¯1/\bar{|A(v)|}. No inductive-miner comparison is attempted, and these numbers are not offered as a process-discovery contribution.
